result.summary: The image shows a residential street undergoing significant road construction, with heavy machinery and traffic cones obstructing the roadway and sightlines. Although sidewalks, pedestrian signals, and marked crosswalks are present, the active work zone and degraded pavement pose immediate safety risks to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Heavy Machinery Obstruction
hazards.description: A large backhoe is positioned in the roadway, blocking sightlines and the direct path of the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, occupying the roadway and intersection area

hazards.name: Excavated Roadway
hazards.description: The road surface is torn up for construction, creating uneven surfaces and tripping hazards for pedestrians crossing the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and middle ground roadway surface

hazards.name: Construction Equipment and Cones
hazards.description: Traffic cones and construction materials clutter the edge of the sidewalk and roadway, narrowing the usable space.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line and sidewalk edge

interventions.title: Temporary Pedestrian Access Route (TPAR)
interventions.description: Establish a clearly marked, protected, and ADA-compliant walkway through the construction zone to separate pedestrians from machinery.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the faded transverse crosswalk markings to high-visibility continental or ladder patterns to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install permanent curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers once construction is complete.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, including a school zone warning sign, visibility is compromised by vehicles parked close to the crossing area.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: The red car on the left and parked cars on the right are positioned very close to the crosswalk, blocking sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Lack of Daylighting
hazards.description: Parking is permitted right up to the crosswalk, which reduces the visibility of pedestrians, particularly children, in this school zone.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and prevent cars from parking too close to the crosswalk, improving visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to slow vehicle speeds and increase pedestrian visibility in a school zone.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps with tactile paving, and signalized control. However, the environment lacks traffic calming measures and visibility is partially hindered by parked vehicles near the crossing points.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection on the right side of the image obstruct the sightlines between pedestrians and approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, adjacent to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Utility Pole and Mailbox Placement
hazards.description: The placement of the utility pole and mailbox on the corner landing narrows the available space for pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines between all road users.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light, reducing conflicts with turning traffic.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and traffic signals within a mixed-use urban environment. While sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the lack of dedicated pedestrian signals and the presence of parked cars near the crossing create potential visibility and safety issues.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may block the view between drivers and pedestrians entering the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street approaching the intersection.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not account for pedestrian clearance intervals.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.
